Grill my schema plan: a React dashboard shows customer cards (name, risk score, open cases) and a case queue with infinite scroll. Data lives in our lakehouse gold layer (star schema) and will sync into a managed Postgres the app reads directly. Case assignments are made in the app.
expected_behavior: asks for the concrete access-pattern inventory (screens/endpoints with filters, sorts, page sizes) before or alongside deeper questions rather than jumping to table shapes

asks prioritized questions drawn from multiple axes (access patterns, keys and sync constraints, freshness SLA, read/write separation for case assignments, tenancy/PII, evolution, failure modes, ownership) instead of dumping an undifferentiated list
flags the app-write concern explicitly: case assignments must live in app-owned writable tables, not in tables replicated from gold
questions are tied to the user's stated context (infinite scroll implies pagination strategy; risk score implies freshness/staleness question)
stays platform-independent, mapping to the user's named stack only as examples

cases.prompt: We want to add a serving schema over our gold layer for a new internal app. That's all we know so far - grill us.
expected_behavior: recognizes the input is too thin and starts with the highest-leverage discovery questions (query inventory, freshness expectations, write paths, tenancy, volumes) rather than inventing assumptions
explains briefly why each early question matters (what failure it prevents)
produces an organized gap list or decision checklist the team can take away
does not produce DDL or a concrete schema design at this stage

cases.prompt: Here are our answers to your grilling: reads are point lookups by customer_id plus one list view sorted by updated_at; freshness must be under 5 minutes; the app writes only annotations; single tenant; PII limited to name/email. What risks remain?
expected_behavior: records or summarizes the answered decisions and derives the remaining open risks from them (e.g., sync mode implications of a 5-minute SLA, index/cursor needs of the sorted list view, where annotations live and how they join to replicated rows, whether name/email even need to be in the serving copy)
distinguishes settled questions from unresolved ones instead of re-asking everything
recommends reviewing the concrete schema once DDL exists (handing off to a schema review) as the natural next step

cases.prompt: Interrogate this design: we plan to point the web app straight at the gold tables in the warehouse to avoid building another layer.
expected_behavior: challenges the direct-to-gold plan with concrete failure modes (latency/concurrency mismatch, coupling of app to warehouse refactors, cost per query, no app write path) phrased as questions or evidence, not dogma
asks what latency, concurrency, and availability the UI actually needs so the decision is grounded in requirements
acknowledges the cases where serving gold directly is acceptable (internal analytics dashboards tolerant of warehouse latency)
